answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks via remote clock-skew fingerprinting of each node's quartz crystal oscillator. Verifiers send periodic timestamped probes to measure microscopic frequency drift, rejecting hollow virtual clones sharing one clock signature. Attackers must dedicate separate physical hardware per identity instead of multiplexing agents on one host. However, a hypervisor can inject synthetic per-VM drift to spoof distinct oscillator profiles.
